title: Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months in exile
deck: The country's best-known opposition leader is back in a state run by a US-backed interim government, and her demand for 2027 elections now sets the clock for a transition that oil investors, Washington and millions of Venezuelans are all watching.

fuel.title: Machado demands 2027 vote, credits Trump
fuel.how: She thanked Trump and Rubio, called for 2027 presidential elections and spoke of an 'organized and peaceful transition', so the question of when the interim government hands over power is now public.

fuel.title: 61 oil deals, $76bn, hinge on stability
fuel.how: Oil companies weighing whether to follow through on signed agreements now have to price a more contested political transition around the interim government.

fuel.title: Young Venezuelans at rally say they will stay
fuel.how: Attendees at a Machado rally said they hold on to hope and do not want to leave, a small sign that her return may slow emigration if hope lasts.

card.headline: Machado's return turns Venezuela's interim period into a race over who sets the election date

keyNumber.label: in exile before María Corina Machado returned on 25 October

forYou.line: The 61 signed oil agreements now sit beside a live political contest; watch whether Washington and Caracas agree on an election timetable.
Political risk around the interim government has changed shape: more legitimacy pressure, but also more chance of conflict over the timetable.
Washington backs both the interim government's deals and Machado's comeback. That balance is the central tension.
Early signs of renewed hope at rallies; whether it cuts emigration depends on jobs and security, not rallies.
Machado wants a presidential election in 2027. Nobody yet has a confirmed date.

effects.text: Machado lands after about 10 months abroad and appears publicly, including on television
She credits Trump and Rubio and says Trump opened a 'floodgate to freedom'
Oil investors re-weigh political risk around the interim government before following through on signed deals
Young Venezuelans at a rally say they hold on to hope and do not want to leave
Acting president Delcy Rodríguez's government faces public pressure to name an election timetable
Washington must balance backing for the interim government's oil deals with support for Machado
Companies may add political-risk clauses or stage commitments until the transition path is clearer (our estimate)
